Property recommendations

Presenting 33 Shetland Drive at its best

A few simple steps before we launch will help the home stand out and give buyers every reason to pay a premium.

01

Managing the tenant exit

We'll manage the tenants' exit from the property for you, including their exit clean, so the home is handed back in top condition ready for launch. We'd also recommend a few small air fresheners through the house so it feels fresh and inviting the moment buyers walk in.

02

Lawns and gardens

Lawns mowed and edged and all garden beds weeded, with watering adjusted as we move into the hotter months. I'm also happy to spread some lawn fertiliser ahead of the next rain to get the lawns looking their best.

03

Styling

We'd definitely recommend styling the home. A styled home is far easier to sell than a vacant one, and styling a house like yours is circa $3,000, an investment that pales in comparison to what it can reflect in the sale price. We're happy to get this properly quoted for you.

Worth knowing

Capital gains tax changes from 1 July 2027

The 2026–27 Federal Budget announced changes to how capital gains are taxed. As an investment property, this is worth factoring into your timing.

01

Inflation-based discount

The current 50 per cent CGT discount is set to be replaced with a discount based on inflation, so tax applies to the real gain after inflation.

02

Minimum 30 per cent rate

A minimum tax rate of 30 per cent is to be introduced on capital gains.

03

Gains from 1 July 2027

The new rules are to apply only to gains that accrue from 1 July 2027 onwards, once those gains are realised.

Selling under the current settings gives you certainty on how your gain will be treated. Everyone's position is different, so we'd recommend a quick chat with your accountant about how the timing of a sale suits you.

Source: The Treasury, Budget 2026–27 tax system changes. These are announced measures and may change before they become law. This is general information only and not tax or financial advice.
